questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Production Operations Runbook”?
options: Assume restarting a container is the same as restoring lost data.
Remove the previous release before validating the replacement.
Plan health evidence, storage, secrets, logs, release identity, and tested recovery before deployment.
Deploy unpinned images and omit backups to keep the setup simple.
questions.answer_key: Plan health evidence, storage, secrets, logs, release identity, and tested recovery before deployment.
questions.explanation: Production operations need reproducibility and recovery evidence; a restart cannot replace a data backup.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering production operations runbook, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to production operations runbook fails, which response is best?
options: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For production operations runbook, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
